items.title: Sea otters have a favourite tool
items.summary: Sea otters use rocks to crack open hard-shelled prey. They can carry rocks and food in loose pockets of skin under their forearms. A tiny example of animal ingenuity.

items.title: We can look billions of years into the past
items.summary: Light takes time to travel. When telescopes observe extremely distant galaxies, they capture light that began its journey billions of years ago. Looking far away is also looking back in time.

items.title: An octopus can solve problems with eight arms
items.summary: Octopus arms contain large networks of neurons that coordinate sensing and movement. Their distributed nervous system is a remarkable example of intelligence unlike our own.

items.title: A museum you can explore from your sofa
items.summary: The Metropolitan Museum of Art makes hundreds of thousands of artworks discoverable online. Try following one object to an unfamiliar period, place, or creative technique.

items.title: A five-second forest break
items.summary: Imagine a quiet path through a forest just after rain. What would you notice first: the smell of the earth, the sound of birds, or the patterns of light? Sometimes a little pause is enough.

items.title: The butterfly with almost invisible wings
items.summary: Glasswing butterflies have transparent areas on their wings. Microscopic structures help reduce reflection, making the wings unusually hard to see against their surroundings.

items.title: The internet's giant open art collection
items.summary: Wikimedia Commons hosts millions of freely licensed and public-domain media files, from historic illustrations to astonishing macro photography. Follow a category and see where it takes you.

items.title: Some birds give gifts
items.summary: Bowerbirds build elaborate structures and arrange colourful objects to attract mates. Different species favour different arrangements — an unexpectedly artistic side of animal behaviour.

items.title: Tonight, the sky is a time machine
items.summary: Every star you see is light arriving from somewhere else in space. Even the nearest stars beyond our Sun are years away at light speed. It's a lovely thought to carry into an evening walk.

items.title: Coral reefs are underwater cities
items.summary: Coral reefs support an astonishing variety of life. Restoration researchers and local communities are experimenting with ways to help damaged reefs recover — complex work worth following.

items.title: What can a building teach us?
items.summary: Buildings are stories about materials, climate, technology, and people. Pick an unfamiliar building and try to guess why it was designed the way it was.

items.title: Why ocean waves are so hypnotic
items.summary: Waves form patterns, but no two moments are quite identical. Take a breath and imagine the slow rhythm of a shoreline. No goal, no productivity requirement — just a pleasant thought.

items.title: A tiny brain teaser
items.summary: No leaderboard, no pressure. Just a small pattern to spot.

game.question: Which of these animals has three hearts?
game.explanation: Octopuses have two hearts that pump blood to the gills and one that pumps it around the body.

game.question: Which planet has the shortest day (fastest rotation)?
game.explanation: Jupiter rotates in roughly ten hours, despite its enormous size.
